Hey all, and welcome to Prompt of the Day. This subverse is about posting mostly picture prompts found across the web and having you, the users, write on them. We’ve had some pretty amazing content so far. However, despite nearly 440 subscribers (WOW! Almost double from last week) and growing at a rate of about 15 users a day, we’ve only got a handful of active writers. Inquisitive, I asked, and a few of you messaged me and stated:

“I want to write, but I don’t know where to begin.”

That’s fine. Now, a good chunk of people will toss out some drivel about “just starting” and “feeling it.” I don’t agree with that philosophy. While It’s easy for some, some of you, like me, focus on every single tiny detail: “Oh, this word sounds weird. Should I use a thesaurus?” “My rhythm is off. I’m not sounding like me.”

Don’t worry, you’re not alone.

So, enough for the Introduction - let’s get started!

Practice 1 - KIS (Keep it Simple)

Imagine you’re a teacher - whatever field, pick something you’re good at- and you have a class full of bright eyed, frightened students. You have a choice here:

a) Scare the ever-loving shit out of them and go on a long tangent about the phylogenetic tree and how its implications on human evolution are both profound and important (e.g. using words no student wants to hear)

or

b) Channel your inner Bill Nye the Science guy and make something complex easy to understand while still teaching.

If you want to go with choice A, then you are either hilarious or evil. Maybe both. But now we’re focusing on choice B.

Using words that are simple to understand, while still effectively conveying a point, is a good starting place. I am not saying that later you can’t use larger, more complex words, but complex emotions, thoughts, and ideas can be expressed simply. Bonus: you can even use more words!

If I give this description:

“Her despondency enveloped her in a somber blanket as she sat in her gloomy parlor. Her face, cold and pallid, never saw the ecstasy of joy in these hollow times.”

Sure, it might sound great if this were England in 1821. But it’s not. Overall it’s a crappy, over-reaching sentence. Instead, what I suggest are using smaller words to convey emotion:

“Her throat seemed to close around her; the tears would come and go, but the stabbing feeling in her gut was something that would never leave. Her limbs felt heavy under her own crushing weight of sadness. Folded up in the tiny chair, the curtains of the room were drawn tightly. Her face, pale and stained with years of crying, never saw the light of joy. Instead, the golden rays of sunlight would bounce away from her in tiny shards, never once allowing her to feel the warmth that she’d felt all those years ago.”

The latter description, while not perfect, conveys a better sense of emotion than the first. The word “despondency” is describing a feeling. So instead of trying to find a single powerful word, I sought to find multiple words to evoke more connectivity to the reader. Despite how complex it may seem (a lot more words), the words are more simple and something we understand. “Stabbing” “shards” “weight” and “heavy.” These are words that allow a reader to picture what’s really going on.

So, keep it simple. Through the simplicity, you’ll find something more complex.

Practice 2-, it’s time to think of an Idea

This is the hardest part of any writing process. So using the methods in Practice 1, let’s think of various ways we can start thinking of an idea! (While we have picture prompts on this sub, it’s important to also develop some skills for later)

The first breakdown is theme. You need to have one. At first it’s going to be difficult to find your “voice.” This is why it’s important to try out a lot of different “themes.” You may have more than one “voice” and that’s okay too.

When deciding your theme, there are a few questions you need to ask. Do you want it to be dark and mysterious? Then maybe a “noir inspired” theme, Do you want it to be exciting and mind blowing? Maybe adventure.

Based on that, you can create your world. City? Country? Future? Past?

After you set your tone, it’s time to work on a simple plot. “There was a murder.” or “Aliens are invading.” -- very simple. Don’t try to conquer the entire plot right now because....

Practice 3 -- making your characters.

First let’s start with your protagonist. Pretend you’ve got a police profile on him or her. Let’s look:

Name: (this can be added later)

[BASIC PROFILE]

Sex:

Date of Birth/Age:

height:

Hair color:

Eye color:

Distinguishing marks: (scars, tattoos, birthmarks go here)

Currently residing:

Occupation:

Alright. Now here’s where it gets fun.

[PERSONALITY AND PSYCHOLOGY]

Meyer Briggs Type : (it’s often fun to take the test answering questions as your main character would)

Psychological disorders: (Do they have depression, anxiety.... sociopathic tendencies? Are they “normal”?)

Temperament: (Are they gloomy, are they cheerful? Are they stony faced and cynical?)

[CHILDHOOD AND HISTORY]

-This one has no specific guidelines. It just really helps to have a basic idea of where your character came from so you know what kind of person he or she is -- For example, I have a lot of small town characters. They’re kind of “folksy” but not idiotic.

Now that you have all of that.... the next step is to have fun. Imagine scenarios where your character has to react.

-What would happen if they were being blackmailed? How would they react? Fight or flight?

-What if someone close to them died?

-what if they were abducted by aliens and then dropped off in the woods 3 days later?

-its their birthday. Someone got them a really stupid gift. How do they react?

That bit is just to get a better feel for your character. Okay. That parts all wrapped up. So Let’s revisit the plot.

Practice 4 - The Plot.

You have your characters. You have a basic theme. You have the ability to write simply and descriptively. Now it’s time to put it to good use. What is your overarching plot point? Now put your character in that world. This is the part where I can’t help you. You have all the basic tools necessary to make your story. Now it’s time to make it come alive.

That’s all Folks

This is just a guide, like I said, so this may not work for you. You can pick and choose what you want to do, you can follow it to a T. There’s no perfect system for creating a good story. Sometimes it just flows out organically, and sometimes you really need a push. Either way, it’s okay. Remember that EVERYTHING posted here is the roughest of drafts. No editing.Sometimes, people won’t like your story. That’s okay. It doesn’t mean you need to give up. It just means that the audience at that time didn’t understand it. Listen to feedback, and don’t take it personally. Instead, use it to build something even better than before.

Alright, this has been gr33narrow with the guide that was promised. I hope you all enjoy this sub and I can’t wait to see the awesome content that will be put out!

If you have any suggestions or tips for new writers, please place them in the comments
